## The R script 

In order to save our work, we will be saving our commands in text files called R scripts. 

Click on File > New File > R Script, or press **Ctrl+Shift+N**

Copy and paste the `setwd()` command from the console to your new R script! 

## Let's do it! 

Now that we have a place to save our program, we can start working with the data. 
We can use a package to help us import functions that will help us read the data into RStudio. 


## How do we access our data file in R?

* If we don't tell R where to look for the file it will guess
* The **working directory** is what we call the default location
* The working directory is where R will look for any input file by default.
* We can tell R where to look by setting the working directory


## Click on Session 

![](slides/images/session_wd.png){height=225px}

## Click on Choose Directory  

![](slides/images/choose_wd.png){height=225px}


## The Console 

After choosing our working directory, you should have seen some code output to the console on the bottom half of your screen: 

![](slides/images/wd_console.png){height=150px}

R generates the command for us to set our working directory, using the `setwd()` function. 

## The Console 

The console is good for seeing results interactively. Try typing this in your console: 

